interest: This document is particularly interesting as a State Department administrative record (Form DS-46) reflecting U.S. diplomatic and military surveillance of Imperial Japanese Navy activities during the tense period of 1933–1934. It captures how consular posts across East and Southeast Asia (Tientsin, Taihoku, Kobe, Singapore, Saigon) and the War Department in Manila tracked Japanese naval movements, including combat patrols along the North China coast between Taku Bar and Shanhaikwan, fleet exercises around Taiwan, long-distance goodwill and training voyages toward the Mediterranean, and probing operations off French Indochina. The sheet also provides valuable insight into State Department cross-referencing practices and inter-agency intelligence coordination prior to World War II.
overview: This file from the U.S. State Department's decimal file 894.33 (Movements of Naval Vessels) consists of a single Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945. The form catalogues and summarizes six documents (sub-numbers 9 through 14) dating from April 1933 to September 1934 regarding the movements, maneuvers, and visits of Imperial Japanese naval vessels. The abstracted reports originate from consular posts in Tientsin, Taihoku, Singapore, Kobe, and Saigon, as well as the War Department via Manila, documenting Japanese naval presence across East and Southeast Asia, including patrols in North China waters between Taku Bar and Shanhaikwan, fleet maneuvers and a royal visit in Taiwan, the voyage of the training cruisers Iwate and Yakumo through Singapore to the Mediterranean, and naval units operating near French Indochina.

subfiles.about: A Department of State List of Papers indexing six communications on Japanese naval vessel movements, maneuvers, and training voyages between April 1933 and September 1934.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State 'List of Papers' (Form DS-46), prepared on October 12, 1945, inventories records filed under decimal file 894.33 regarding Japanese naval vessel movements. The entries summarize six reports (sub-numbers 9 through 14) from consular posts in Tientsin, Taihoku, Singapore, Kobe, and Saigon, alongside an intelligence report from the War Department forwarded from Manila. Key topics documented include warship patrols off the North China coast between Taku Bar and Shanhaikwan, Imperial fleet visits and maneuvers in Taiwan and Keelung, the transit of the training cruisers Iwate and Yakumo through Singapore en route to the Mediterranean, and naval activity near French Indochina.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Movements of Japanese Naval Vessels
